 UFC Qatar: Shamil Gaziev vs. Tallison Teixeira Predictions & Odds
 Anatoly Pimentel 
 Nov 20, 2026, 4:45 AM 
 min read 
 (AP Photo/Altaf Qadri) 
 The thrilling heavyweight showdown between Shamil Gaziev and Tallison Teixeira will be part of the UFC Qatar card on Saturday at ABHA Arena in Doha. 
 Fresh off a bounce-back victory in his previous fight, Gaziev is going to be the betting favorite with -200 UFC odds , while Teixeira, who absorbed a defeat in his last bout, will be the betting underdog with +165 odds. 
 UFC Qatar: Shamil Gaziev vs. Tallison Teixeira Fight Odds 
 Shamil Gaziev: -200 
 Tallison Teixeira: +165 
 UFC Qatar: Shamil Gaziev vs. Tallison Teixeira: Tale of the Tape

 UFC Qatar: Shamil Gaziev vs. Tallison Teixeira: Prediction 
 My prediction is a TKO/KO victory for Gaziev over Teixeira because he’s the more powerful puncher with a slightly better chin. Even though Gaziev gives up the physical traits to Teixeira, he’s still better at closing distance. 
 Teixeira uses his reach well, spamming jabs against opponents since he’s usually the taller, longer fighter. But when he’s pressed forward, he tends to panic, and that is where he makes mistakes that open up opportunities for opponents to land clean shots. 
 As the shorter fighter, Gaziev is expected to put Teixeira on the back foot from the get-go. This will help him close the gap before he throws his signature overhand punch, which could put Teixeira down. My only concern is whether Gaziev gets hit first as he lunges forward. 
 Shamil Gaziev’s Recent Fight Results 
 Gaziev was an undefeated fighter when he joined Dana White’s Contender Series in 2023 and secured a contract. In his last five bouts, he recorded three wins (Don’Tale Mayes, Thomas Petersen, and Kennedy Nzechukwu) and two losses (Waldo Cortes Acosta and Brando Pericic). 
 Tallison Teixeira’s Recent Fight Results 
 Teixeira is also a product of Dana White’s Contender Series in 2024 as an undefeated prospect. But he has split his first four bouts inside the octagon, beating Justin Tafa and Tai Tuivasa but losing to Derrick Lewis and Sergei Pavlovich.
